reference.title: Barbell Incline Shoulders Press (male)
reference.listing: Video (title and product number from the listing URL; the page itself could not be read from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as the bar lowers, breathe out as you press.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s down, a light touch, about 1.2 s up

prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen: between your seated overhead press and your incline bench press. Leave about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8).
prescription.progression: Add 2.5 kg when every rep reaches the upper chest and locks out over the shoulders.

cues.text: Back pad steep (about 60 degrees), buttocks back in the seat, head and upper back on the pad, feet planted. Overhand grip a little wider than the shoulders; take the bar out to straight arms over the shoulders.
Lower the bar to the top of the chest just under the chin, forearms vertical, elbows a little in front of the bar.
Touch lightly at the collarbones; head stays on the pad.
Press straight up to locked arms over the shoulders; breathe out.
Steady the bar before the next rep.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the lower back off the pad
mistakes.fix: Keep the ribs down and the buttocks back in the seat.

mistakes.mistake: Bar drifting forward over the face
mistakes.fix: Press straight up over the shoulders.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows flaring straight out to the sides
mistakes.fix: Keep them a little in front of the bar.

kinematics.norm: Steep incline (about 60 degrees): front deltoid activity rises and upper-chest share falls as the bench approaches vertical (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020)
A little wider than the shoulders (common coaching)
About 90 degrees or more at the bottom (clinical opinion)
From the upper chest to over the shoulders (common coaching)

sources.title: GymVisual, Barbell Incline Shoulders Press (male), video (movement reference only)

Rodríguez-Ridao, Antequera-Vique, Martín-Fuentes and Muyor 2020, effect of five bench inclinations on the electromyographic activity of the pectoralis major, anterior deltoid and triceps brachii during the bench press exercise (Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(19):7339; PMC7579505)

cautions: Press inside a rack with safeties or with a spotter; never press heavy alone without safeties.
Lower the bar to the chest, not behind the head.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder pain: lower the bench to 45 degrees or shorten the range.
Lower-back discomfort: buttocks back and ribs down.

muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Main mover: front-deltoid activity rises as the bench gets steeper (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Main mover: front-deltoid activity rises as the bench gets steeper (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020).
muscleNotes.pec_r: Upper (clavicular) fibres help at the bottom; their share falls as the incline steepens toward vertical (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020).
muscleNotes.pec_l: Upper (clavicular) fibres help at the bottom; their share falls as the incline steepens toward vertical (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straighten the elbows to lock out.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Straighten the elbows to lock out.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Helps raise the arms as the bar goes overhead.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Helps raise the arms as the bar goes overhead.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Rotates the shoulder blades upward as the arms rise.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Rotates the shoulder blades upward as the arms rise.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Help rotate the shoulder blades upward at the top.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Help rotate the shoulder blades upward at the top.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Hold the upper back against the pad.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Hold the upper back against the pad.
